# Draft and AC integrity gate: acme/widgets CSV export latency (repair)

## Step 4 - Draft: full replacement body

```markdown
## Context
Requesters export reports as CSV from the widgets app. The current p95 export latency is 5s for the representative 100-row report, measured in the recorded request-timing run.

## Problem
Requesters wait 5s at p95 for a 100-row CSV export instead of the required maximum of 2s.

## Idea
The reporter proposes improving CSV export in acme/widgets.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Given the representative 100-row report, when CSV exports of it are requested and timed with the baseline request-timing method (request to file ready), then p95 export latency is <= 2s (baseline 5s, from the recorded request-timing run).

## Post-deployment housekeeping
Non-blocking: monitor export latency after release.
```

**Changes from the current body:**

- **AC row rewritten under the deploy-window rule.** The old row said "in staging". AC rows must not name an environment, so the venue is left to the spec. The row now states setup, action and observable result.
- **"Measurement clarification" section removed.** It is not a permitted section. Its whole content now sits in the AC row: the same request-timing method, the representative 100-row report, request-to-file-ready latency, and the supplied baseline and target. Nothing was dropped, so this is not displaced detail.
- **Preserved unchanged:**
  - the 2s target
  - the 5s baseline
  - the non-blocking Post-deployment housekeeping section
- **Single repo (acme/widgets).** The AC list stays flat, with no repo groups.
- **Idea** stays within its one attributed sketch line, so there is no overflow.
- **Reporter-note comment:** none proposed. There is no overflow, no step-5 move, no AC uniqueness removal, and no in-session ask.

## AC integrity gate (assembled draft)

**Normalize:** there is one criterion, already a `- [ ]` item. This is a substantive repair because the AC text changed, so there is no byte lock.

**Uniqueness:** there is one row with a single observation, so there is nothing to remove or split.

| AC | Class test | Result |
|---|---|---|
| p95 export latency <= 2s (baseline 5s), representative 100-row report, baseline request-timing method | **Comparative.** Baseline: 5s, citable today from the recorded request-timing run. Target: <= 2s. Measurement: request to file ready at p95, same method as baseline. All three are supplied values, not estimates. | **Pass**: not wishful |
| same | Not tautological (no self-produced set), not unspecified-but-binding (the value is given), no external-input dependency | **Pass** |
| same | Deploy-window: verifiable before production with the representative report; no environment named | **Pass**: stays an AC |
| Post-deployment housekeeping: "monitor export latency after release" | Prod-only observation | Correctly kept as non-blocking housekeeping, not an AC |

**Outcome:** no hard stop and no park, so the draft proceeds to step 5.

**Carried to step 8 (Evidence gate):** the Problem example has no `source:` footer, and the title is non-discovery. That makes it a source gap. At gate-open it will be prefilled as `source: none (not recorded at filing)` and shown in the old->new diff, rendered as `source missing: Requesters wait 5s at p95 for a 100-row CSV export`. The write is still offered.

## Replacement body

```markdown
## Context
Requesters export reports as CSV from the widgets app. The recorded baseline is 5s at p95 for the representative 100-row report, measuring the time from requesting an export until its file is ready. The baseline and required 2s target are supplied values, not estimates.

## Problem
Requesters wait 5s at p95 for a 100-row CSV export instead of the required maximum of 2s.

## Idea
The reporter proposes improving CSV export in acme/widgets.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Given the representative 100-row report, when CSV exports are measured using the same request-timing method as the recorded baseline, p95 request-to-file-ready latency is at most 2s, compared with the recorded 5s baseline.

## Post-deployment housekeeping
Non-blocking: monitor export latency after release.
```

**AC integrity gate: pass.** The comparative criterion retains the supplied baseline, target, representative input, and measurement method. It specifies setup, action, and an observable result verifiable before production deployment. The staging restriction is removed from the AC; the verification venue belongs in the implementation specification. Post-release monitoring remains explicitly non-blocking.

**Proposed comment:** none; no detail was displaced.
